note: The thirteen tasks of the IAEval paper (Build, Test, Success), copied verbatim from evals/build-tasks.json on 2026-10-21. `post` are the machine-checked requirements of Sec. 3.6.4. The seven-task ablation subset is marked.

tasks.prompt: Build a straight wall 16 studs long, 1 stud thick, at least 6 bricks tall, with a doorway opening in the middle (at least 3 studs wide and 5 bricks tall) spanned by a lintel. Use running-bond brick courses (seams overlapped). One color for the wall, another for the lintel. 30-70 parts.

Build a square watchtower: footprint about 6x6 studs, at least 10 bricks tall, with a wider battlement platform on top (about 8x8 studs, with a parapet ring around its edge). Two colors maximum, sensible courses with overlapped seams (running bond), no floating parts. 60-120 parts.

Build a small house: rectangular footprint about 8x10 studs, walls at least 5 bricks tall with a doorway in one long wall and one window opening in another, topped by a sloped gable roof made of slope bricks. Two or three colors, walls in running bond, roof in a single color. 60-140 parts.

Build a stepped pyramid: square base about 12x12 studs, at least 5 tiers, each tier inset by one stud on every side, in a single sand-colored scheme. Center the tiers so nothing overhangs. 60-140 parts.

Build a tall lighthouse on a rocky base: a rough wide base (about 8x8 studs, 2-3 bricks, dark grey), then a tapering tower in alternating red and white bands at least 14 bricks tall, topped by a glazed lantern room (trans-clear pieces) with a small roof. It must stand: keep the tower centered over the base as it tapers. Within a 10x10 stud footprint. 80-180 parts.

Build a section of Roman aqueduct: a lower tier of at least 4 round arches (arch bricks or corbelled), a second tier of smaller arches above it, and a water channel running along the top with side walls. Straight run, about 24 studs long, 3-4 studs thick. Tan/sand scheme. 100-220 parts.

Build a Greek temple: a stepped stylobate base about 16x10 studs, a colonnade of at least 6 round columns per long side (freestanding, evenly spaced), an inner cella wall, an entablature beam ring resting on the columns, and a low-pitch pediment roof with triangular gable ends. Sand or white scheme. 120-260 parts.

Build the Great Pyramid: square base 14x14 studs, at least 7 tiers stepping in evenly to a peak, in tan, with one side carrying a small entrance opening at ground level. Center the tiers exactly. 130-280 parts.

Build a Colosseum-style arena: a closed oval or octagonal ring wall about 20x16 studs outside, with a lower tier of arched openings all the way around and a second, set-back tier above with smaller openings. Sand color. Leave the arena floor open. 150-320 parts.

Build an extremely detailed model of Notre-Dame de Paris: two rectangular west towers with tall arched openings, a large rose window above three portal arches between them, a long nave behind with flying buttresses along both sides, and a slender spire at the crossing. Use trans-colored pieces for stained glass — the rose window and the tall nave windows should glow with mixed trans colors. Light grey stone with a dark roof. 450-900 parts.

Build a detailed Taj Mahal: a wide raised platform, a central hall with a great arched iwan on each face, a large central onion dome on a drum, four smaller domed kiosks around it, and four slender corner minarets with little domes. All white with subtle accents. 450-900 parts.

This is the official LEGO Halloween Ghost, loaded as-is. Build a black display pedestal (at least 6x6 studs, 3 bricks tall, one row of dark-grey trim) and put the ghost ON TOP of it. The engine cannot move placed parts, so to lift the ghost you must remove its parts and re-place the SAME arrangement higher up — record the original positions first (inspect_build), and rebuild it exactly, only translated. The final scene must contain the complete unchanged ghost (same parts, same colors, same relative arrangement) standing on the pedestal.

You may use ONLY the parts remaining in your inventory — every placement is rejected once a part+color runs out (check remaining stock with inspect_build). From this inventory, build a DINOSAUR: a standing four-legged or two-legged dinosaur with a long neck or big head, a tail, and a recognizable silhouette from the side. It must be valid and stable. Use the silhouette tool to check the side view reads as a dinosaur.
